area_title: Staging/performance/cleanup plus IDataReader/custom-reader validation/retry tradeoff tail
what_area_is_about: when SqlBulkCopy should target a staging table instead of the final table
performance controls: TableLock, BatchSize, indexes, triggers, transaction log pressure and streaming large files
staging-table shapes: heap staging, shared staging tables, temporary tables and import identifiers
cleanup strategies: drop table, delete successful rows, batch cleanup, cleanup inside/outside transaction
failed-row handling: keep failed rows, move errors to a separate table/path, identify bad rows after bulk operations
IDataReader/custom reader tradeoffs: streaming, custom CSV readers, DbDataReader, validation/error reporting, retry complexity and one-pass limitations
key_ideas: R01 explained the API; R02/R03 explain production import strategy around that API.
A staging table is the safer place for validation, transformation, deduplication, merge/upsert and failed-row isolation.
Performance is not one flag: indexes, triggers, batch size, locks and transaction-log pressure all interact.
Cleanup must be designed before the import: shared table with import id, temp table, drop table, delete-success rows, or move failures aside.
Custom IDataReader/DbDataReader streaming can reduce memory and support DB-to-DB or CSV streams, but validation, retries and error reporting become harder.
Custom readers are not automatically faster for small/medium imports; simplicity may beat one-pass streaming unless scale requires it.
